description: Closure of an event under a stop predicate means: some set contains it, and each set member stops or has one admitted record with all contributors and enablers in the set. Inductive closure is #734 Supply with every member demanded. Inductive closure gives closure and contributor Supply, and without enablers Supply gives inductive closure; failure of inductive closure is exactly membership in a borrowing trap of the all-member groups; a well-founded membership graph, or an acyclic one on a finite carrier, makes every closed event inductively closed. Each member of an accounted set has inductive closure or else an infinite descent in that set with no full supply, on which some member is its own ancestor or no member repeats; the two options exclude each other at that member. In a coherent exercise whose exercised records have a member, closure of every contingent event with stops at occurrence in every allowed scenario is equivalent to the contingent-fact PSR of an arena whose reasons are members of exercised records, an analyst stipulation; stop-free closure of every occurring event is equivalent to that arena's fact PSR; a record with no member breaks the first equivalence forward, and an incoherent exercise breaks it backward. Closure of one target that is not necessary in the scenario space, all of whose exercised records list every other contingent event, gives the contingent-fact PSR when exercised records have a member. A #750 reason-closed account in that arena yields closure, and the converse fails in a fixed cycle model. For a contingent event of a coherent exercise at least one holds, with possible overlap: a contingent ancestor with no exercised record; an infinite descent in some accounted set; an exercised ancestor record not jointly sufficient. Fixed controls have each option alone. Inductive closure with stops occurring at every allowed scenario and a target not doing so gives an incomplete ancestor record; if all exercised records are sufficient the target occurs at every allowed scenario; with scenarios and worlds matching in both directions the first statement holds for stops necessary at a world and a target contingent there. A fixed joint group a, b, c with enabler p, complete and with each member indispensable, has contributor Supply of its effect d from a source under four record sets. With nothing recorded for p, d lacks closure at stops occurring in every allowed scenario, has inductive closure when p is added as a stop, and that model lacks the contingent-fact PSR although a is closed. With p recorded from the source d has inductive closure and the PSR holds; the occurrence table is the same in these two models. With an infinite chain or a two-event cycle behind p, d is closed and the PSR holds, without inductive closure. In the cycle, the component of p and q has Supply in the condensation with no intrinsic event. The first model restricted to the actual scenario has closure of d and p is not indispensable. Under joint sufficiency a member occurring at every allowed scenario is not an indispensable condition; closure gives indispensable closure, and a fixed overdetermination model has the latter without the former. This establishes consequences in the encoded record and scenario semantics. It does not establish that an explanation must be closed, that any stop is legitimate, that any record is productive, that any PSR is true, the existence of bearers, or any root premise.
